hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6409.meaning: When people ignore their duties and roles, confusion spreads. We find peace by doing our best in our own path and respecting others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6409.context: Social roles become reversed as scholars stop chanting and others take their place. The natural order of society begins to decay.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6696.meaning: This verse tells the story of a man who feels at ease and shows his lotus flower to his horse while sitting by a lake. It symbolizes finding peace and connecting with nature.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6696.context: In the Hindu epic Mahabharata, this verse describes a scene where a man feels relieved and places his lotus flower in front of his horse before sitting by a lake's bank.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6697.meaning: The man hears a beautiful song, highlighting the soothing and serene atmosphere around him.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6697.context: Continuing the narrative from verse 1, this verse mentions the man hearing a pleasant sound.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6698.meaning: This verse portrays the man wondering about the singer of the song, reflecting on the mystery and beauty of the moment.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6698.context: The verse continues the story, showing the man pondering the source of the song.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6699.meaning: This verse introduces a beautiful maiden who is singing and picking flowers, creating a magical atmosphere.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6699.context: The man sees a stunning maiden picking flowers and singing.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6700.meaning: This verse shows the man approaching the enchanting maiden and inquiring about her name, beginning a conversation.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6700.context: The man approaches the maiden and asks her identity.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6701.meaning: Arthi introduces herself as the singer and mentions that the man can only meet her near the lake.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6701.context: The maiden reveals her name as Arthi and tells the man she can only be found at the lake.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6703.meaning: This verse depicts the man agreeing to meet Arthi by the lake, showing his willingness to seek her presence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6703.context: The man agrees to follow Arthi to the lake.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6704.meaning: The verse reveals that Arthi informs the man that he will meet her near the lake, emphasizing the importance of the location.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_6704.context: Arthi tells the man that he will find her again at the lake.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7195.meaning: Simple physical experiences are sacred gifts. We should appreciate the beauty found in everyday sensory interactions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7195.context: The text describes how basic senses like sound and touch come from the divine earth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7197.meaning: Our senses connect us to the divine. Recognizing this link helps us see the sacred in all things.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7197.context: Sensory experiences are described as waves of divine light reflecting the greatness of the supreme creator.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7198.meaning: Understanding how nature works reveals deeper truths. We learn to respect the subtle forces around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7198.context: The verse explains how sound and touch exist within the air, showing the nature of elements.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7199.meaning: Life is a cycle of change. We must accept that our physical form is temporary and changing.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7199.context: When living and non-living things act in balance, the soul moves to a new body later.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7201.meaning: Change is the only constant in life. We should accept impermanence and flow with natural cycles.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7201.context: Material elements are constantly being destroyed and reborn, covering everything in the world around us.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7202.meaning: Look beyond what you see. True wisdom comes from understanding the invisible spiritual reality behind life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7202.context: Things we see are real, but the unseen spiritual truth is also real and beyond senses.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7203.meaning: Mastering your reactions brings peace. Controlling your senses helps you avoid unnecessary suffering and stress.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7203.context: When a person controls their senses properly, they do not suffer pain or distress in life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7204.meaning: We are connected to everything. Seeing the divine in others helps us love and respect all beings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7204.context: A wise person sees the divine in the world and the world within themselves.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7625.meaning: It reminds us that generosity can repeat itself, creating many kinds of good people in the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7625.context: A speaker says people will be different kinds, and Ashivasha and Shivasha are generous again and again.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7626.meaning: It shows that mothers can choose to follow their children’s example, learning new strengths from them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7626.context: Mothers come to Sakanda, deciding to become like their sons Kaki, Halima, Rudra, and Brihali.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7627.meaning: Even strong or scary children can teach us that power comes with responsibility and care.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7627.context: Women have a powerful baby named Shira, who is terrible, and Sakanda’s son Parsadaja has red eyes.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7628.meaning: Heroes can come from many families, and unusual traits can still bring honor and bravery.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7628.context: Eight heroes are mentioned, born from Sakanda’s mothers, and a new one with a goat’s mouth appears.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7629.meaning: Mothers honor leaders who show many qualities, believing that many strengths help guide people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7629.context: The sixth goat’s mouth belongs to Sakanda; the king has six heads, worshiped by mothers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7630.meaning: Great leaders use their voice to bring good, showing that speaking wisely can create positive change.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7630.context: The best of the six is praised for his powerful voice, creating the divine Bhadrashakha.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7631.meaning: Mothers respect leaders with many talents, believing that many gifts help protect and guide families.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7631.context: Again, the sixth goat’s mouth is Sakanda’s; the six-headed king is worshiped by mothers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7632.meaning: Mothers honor leaders who show many strengths, trusting that many qualities bring safety and hope.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7632.context: The sixth goat’s mouth is Sakanda’s; the king’s six heads are worshiped by mothers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7660.meaning: Birth can come from powerful actions, showing that great deeds bring new life and hope.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7660.context: A baby horse is born from Rudra after he enters a fire, then Sakanda, Rudra's son, is born.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7661.meaning: Divine help and teamwork create powerful beings, teaching that cooperation leads to greatness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7661.context: Six women, guided by Rudra's fire, bring forth Sakanda, the best of the gods, and Rudra's son is born.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7662.meaning: Radiant strength and bright energy inspire others, showing that confidence shines through challenges.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7662.context: The son of the fire wears red clothes, his body shines like the sun with red clouds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7663.meaning: Symbols of power and protection remind us that courage and faith can guard us in difficult times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7663.context: A chicken is given by the fire, its flag is decorated, and the chariot looks red like black fire.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7664.meaning: Preparedness and resilience help us face battles, teaching that readiness brings victory.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7664.context: He enters armor, his body moves easily, and always appears another part of the body fighting.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7665.meaning: True protection comes from inner power and honesty, not from false beliefs or tricks.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7665.context: Shakti, shield, strength, splendor, loveliness, truth, and injury protect devotees without delusion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7666.meaning: Powerful forces can both destroy harm and safeguard life, showing balance in strength.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7666.context: The destruction of enemies and protection of worlds are born with Sakanda, the lord of men.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7667.meaning: Celebration and beauty honor achievements, reminding us to appreciate and celebrate good deeds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7667.context: He is consecrated and adorned by all gods, flowers shine, and the full moon is seen.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7857.meaning: The verse warns that weapons and cruel speech can cause great harm, teaching us to avoid violence and gossip.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7857.context: A warrior’s sword is described as very dangerous, and people who wish to harm others spread harmful words.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7859.meaning: It reminds us that harsh words can damage our inner self, so we should speak kindly and gently.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7859.context: The tongue is compared to a skin that can be harmed, and harmful powders will surely kill the spirit.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7860.meaning: The passage shows how neglect and bad influences can weaken a person’s strength and awareness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7860.context: People are described as being covered in water, made weak by women, and losing senses like sight and hearing.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7861.meaning: It encourages following noble examples and listening to honest teachings for a better life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7861.context: The speaker says they follow the same actions as the great Pandavas, urging Satyabhama to listen to truth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7863.meaning: It teaches that letting go of selfish feelings and helping others leads to peace and respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7863.context: The speaker says they always leave ego, desire, and anger behind and serve the Pandavas and their families.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7864.meaning: The verse shows how pain can make people feel helpless, reminding us to offer comfort and understanding.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7864.context: A woman looks at a man in distress, and her thoughts are filled with sorrow and confusion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7866.meaning: It highlights the value of loyalty and strength in protecting others and standing up for justice.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7866.context: A warrior named Suryavaishvanara serves the Parthas and is described as powerful and fierce.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7867.meaning: It suggests that true worth comes from inner qualities, not from outward roles or titles.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_7867.context: The verse lists a god, a man, a gandharva, and a young man, noting no other man is a doorman or character.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8043.meaning: It shows the king’s careful management and pride in his large herd, teaching responsibility for resources.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8043.context: The king counted many cows, marking each with his fingers and large numbers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8044.meaning: New life brings joy and abundance, reminding us that growth often comes from humble beginnings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8044.context: A calf was born in a mother’s lap, and the herd spread across the fields.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8045.meaning: Fun and play can lift spirits, showing that joy is a divine gift for all people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8045.context: Soldiers and townspeople played in the forest, acting like gods in their games.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8047.meaning: Music and beauty unite people, teaching that celebration strengthens community bonds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8047.context: Cowherd men sang and danced, while Dhritarashtra approached and women were decorated.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8048.meaning: Generosity brings happiness, illustrating that sharing blessings creates lasting goodwill.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8048.context: The king, surrounded by wives, shared wealth, giving food and drink to many.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8049.meaning: Nature’s diversity shows that all creatures belong together, encouraging respect for every life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8049.context: People gathered with trees, buffaloes, deer, cows, bears, and boars in the forest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8050.meaning: Hunting requires skill and respect, reminding us to use resources wisely and responsibly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8050.context: He shot arrows, tied animals, and hunted deer in beautiful forest places.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8051.meaning: Nature’s beauty invites awe, teaching us to appreciate and protect the environment around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8051.context: The text mentions forests with beautiful flowering trees and a call to observe them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9149.meaning: The task ahead is huge and covers many different places, so you need to be brave and ready.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9149.context: The monkeys describe the vast land with forests, mountains, and cities that they must search.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9150.meaning: Deadlines help us stay focused and move quickly, so do not waste time on your important goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9150.context: Rama sets a strict time limit for the search mission before they take further action.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9151.meaning: Letting go of anger helps you stay humble and keeps your relationships strong and peaceful with others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9151.context: A wise monkey leader calms down and shows respect to Sugriva after a moment of anger.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9152.meaning: Looking at things from a higher perspective helps you understand the situation better and plan wisely.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9152.context: Sugriva and Rama climb a high mountain to get a better view of the land.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9153.meaning: Working together in teams allows you to cover more ground and find what you are looking for.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9153.context: The monkey chiefs gather in large groups to search in three directions, excluding the south.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9154.meaning: Sometimes you will not find what you seek right away, but you must keep trying and not give up.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9154.context: The monkeys report back that they searched the land but could not find Sita or Ravana.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9155.meaning: Having hope in your team gives you strength, even when you feel worried about the outcome.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9155.context: The monkey leaders head south while Rama watches them with hope and concern for his wife.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9156.meaning: It is important to communicate your results promptly so leaders can make the next best decision.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9156.context: After two weeks, the searchers return quickly to Sugriva to report their findings to him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9297.meaning: Even strong warriors can fall in battle. Death comes to everyone eventually, so do not rely only on physical power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9297.context: Monkeys in the story were seen fighting far away. They were strong but died and fell to the ground.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9298.meaning: Anger often leads to rash actions. When we lose control, we ignore the peace around us and cause trouble.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9298.context: Ravana felt angry and could not stand the situation. He went out to fight while deer ate in the woods.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9299.meaning: Preparation and duty come before action. Completing your responsibilities properly sets the stage for success and order.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9299.context: Rama arrived with a large army of warriors. He had finished a special ritual before the nightingale sang again.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9300.meaning: Conflict often involves many people. When sides clash, allies join in, making the situation bigger and more complex.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9300.context: Ravana met Rama for a big fight. Lakshmana fought Jita while Indra joined the battle on the other side.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9301.meaning: Victory is not guaranteed for anyone. Even leaders can lose, showing that strength alone does not decide every outcome.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9301.context: Sugriva lost to Virupaksha. Tara and others fought with their weapons. The battle was fierce and chaotic for all.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9302.meaning: Overconfidence can lead to danger. Relying only on your tools or strength without wisdom often brings unexpected problems.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9302.context: One who thought things were okay faced trouble. He relied on his many weapons and strength in the fight.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9303.meaning: Violence creates fear and awe. Powerful actions can shock everyone, reminding us of the serious impact of our deeds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9303.context: A powerful blow increased fear in the weak. The scene was terrifying, like the awe felt by gods and demons.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9304.meaning: Attacks often meet strong resistance. When you strike with force, expect a powerful counterattack from your opponent.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9304.context: Ravana threw many spears and swords at Rama. Rama fought back by hitting Ravana with sharp iron rods.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9635.meaning: True leaders show empathy and try to comfort those who are suffering from great personal pain.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9635.context: The king feels deep sadness after hearing the sad news about the bride and her loss.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9636.meaning: Sometimes life presents difficult challenges that seem impossible to solve, requiring patience and careful thought.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9636.context: The king tells the princess that finding a home for three people is a very hard task.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9637.meaning: We should trust our own ability to overcome problems and reassure loved ones that we are okay.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9637.context: Savitri tells her father not to worry because she will handle the situation with strength and care.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9638.meaning: We must respect our commitments and promises, even when they are hard to keep or change later.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9638.context: The father admits he cannot ask his daughter to give up her special wish or promise to the gods.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9639.meaning: Deep sorrow can make us feel frozen and unable to move, showing how powerful human emotions can be.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9639.context: The father stops talking, and Savitri stands still, looking like a piece of wood in her grief.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9640.meaning: Grief is a natural part of life, and we often need time to sit with our pain before moving on.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9640.context: Savitri spends the whole night in deep sadness after her husband died, waiting for the morning to come.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9641.meaning: Daily spiritual practices help us stay connected to our values and maintain a sense of order in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9641.context: The text describes performing morning fire rituals at sunrise, which are important for spiritual life and duty.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9642.meaning: Even powerful beings show humility and respect when facing serious matters or higher spiritual truths.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9642.context: Old gods in heaven stand with folded hands, showing deep respect and humility before the great event.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9854.meaning: True friendship with the divine is the highest gift, showing that God can appear in any form to help you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9854.context: A divine being reveals their true identity to a devotee during a moment of deep spiritual connection.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9855.meaning: God offers endless love and friendship to everyone, showing that divine care is boundless and always available to you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9855.context: The speaker declares their vast capacity for love and friendship to the person they are addressing.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9856.meaning: If you truly want to help others, you must listen carefully to wise words that guide you toward good actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9856.context: A wise figure speaks to a listener, emphasizing the importance of caring for the well being of others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9857.meaning: Life is precious and connected to higher powers, reminding us that our existence has a deeper purpose and value.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9857.context: A woman speaks about her pregnancy and her role in supporting the gods and holding her own life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9859.meaning: Even powerful gods may humble themselves to seek help, teaching us that no one is too important to ask for support.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9859.context: A speaker addresses a brahmin, mentioning that Indra might come in disguise to ask for help for the Pandavas.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9860.meaning: Generosity and fame are linked, showing that giving to others can protect your reputation and ensure you are remembered well.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9860.context: The speaker promises to give valuable items like earrings and a shield to a visitor, ensuring their fame remains.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9861.meaning: It is better to die with honor and fame than to live without purpose, teaching us that dignity matters more than survival.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9861.context: A warrior reflects on the value of life versus fame, deciding that dying with honor is more important than living.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9862.meaning: We should be ready to share our best possessions with those in need, showing that true wealth is found in giving.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9862.context: The speaker decides to give their treasures to Indra if a specific person comes to them asking for alms.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10063.meaning: This sets the scene for a story about a couple who really wanted a baby very much.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10063.context: A king had a very beautiful wife named Radha who did not have any children yet.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10064.meaning: Nature often brings unexpected gifts to our lives when we least expect them to arrive.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10064.context: A beautiful box floated down the river and was carried by the strong and stormy waves.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10065.meaning: Curiosity can lead us to discover wonderful things that change our lives for the better.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10065.context: The woman felt curious about the box and grabbed it to see what was inside.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10066.meaning: Sometimes the most precious things are hidden in plain sight or found in unexpected places.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10066.context: They pulled the box out of the water and opened it to find a baby inside.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10067.meaning: True beauty and worth come from within a person, not just from what they wear.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10067.context: The baby looked like a young sun and wore a golden shield on his body.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10068.meaning: Love and joy can fill a home instantly when a new life arrives in it.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10068.context: The parents were shocked and happy to see the baby and held him close to them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10069.meaning: We often feel that special moments in life are guided by a higher power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10069.context: The mother felt the baby was shy and thought the gods had sent him to her.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10070.meaning: Gratitude and faith help us accept blessings that seem to come from a divine source.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_10070.context: The father believed the gods gave them this son because they had no children before.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_501.meaning: People who choose evil paths face rejection and should be stopped to protect the innocent and good.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_501.context: A wicked man follows his bad desires and is rejected by society for his evil actions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_502.meaning: You must keep doing good things every day to stay strong and keep your good name.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_502.context: If people stop doing good deeds, their moral strength fades away and they lose their honor.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_503.meaning: When we care for and protect the vulnerable, everyone in the group stays safe and happy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_503.context: Protecting women in society helps keep the whole community safe and the spirit of people pure.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_504.meaning: Your role in life is to fight for justice and protect others from those who harm them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_504.context: Priests talk about rules, but warriors have a different job to do in times of conflict.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_505.meaning: It is wrong to watch someone get hurt and do nothing to help them when you can.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_505.context: A woman tells a hero how a bad man hurt her while he was right there.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_506.meaning: True friends will stand by you and fight hard to keep you safe from danger.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_506.context: A powerful warrior promises to save his friends and defeat the enemies who threaten them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_507.meaning: We should ask for forgiveness when we are wrong and try to heal broken relationships with others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_507.context: A person asks for forgiveness because they feel hurt and despised by someone else in the story.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_508.meaning: Giving in to bad desires causes trouble for everyone and should be broken like a pot.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_508.context: A hero tells a villain that their lust is like darkness that brings bad luck.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_736.meaning: Speed and unity can overcome many enemies if you act together.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_736.context: Lord meets Kauravas, crosses river quickly, takes them all together.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_737.meaning: Plan carefully, then act decisively to secure power and safety.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_737.context: Suggests making a treaty to control a man, then kill his army.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_738.meaning: Success comes when you manage others well and grow stronger together.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_738.context: Promises happiness by controlling a man, expecting growth in strength.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_739.meaning: Listening to wise words can guide leaders to make good choices.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_739.context: Karna speaks to king after hearing words, praising Susharma.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_740.meaning: Swift action and sharing tools can help achieve a noble goal.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_740.context: They leave quickly, add Varuthi, split the bow, call it sinless.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_741.meaning: Respecting elders and teachers brings wisdom and guidance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_741.context: Describes grandfather of Kurus, teacher, and other wise men.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_742.meaning: Good planning and invitations lead to successful meetings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_742.context: Plans a journey, invites someone, then meets the king.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_743.meaning: Without resources and bravery, one cannot achieve great goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_743.context: Questions the Pandavas' lack of wealth, strength, and courage.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_718.meaning: Great leaders pass away but new heroes rise with passion and power to face the challenges of their time.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_718.context: Ancient warriors retired long ago. Now the Pandavas are eager and ready with their splendid horses for battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_719.meaning: Society needs clear rules for power and money. Leaders must establish these standards to keep order and peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_719.context: We must set rules for strength, wealth, and good behavior. We will fix these things properly when the time is right.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_720.meaning: True strength means supporting your allies and protecting those who are vulnerable. You must be brave for everyone around you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_720.context: Know your own strength well. Be strong with your friends and also be strong when helping the weak people.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_721.meaning: Life involves judging others and being judged. Understanding power dynamics helps us navigate the complex relationships between people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_721.context: We understand different levels of power. We decided the fate of others and others decided our fate in the past.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_722.meaning: Leaders must balance kindness with firmness. Use fairness for most but apply necessary force to protect the vulnerable from harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_722.context: He treated people with fairness and charity. He used justice for some and force for the weak to maintain order.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_723.meaning: Even if enemies seem strong, their weaknesses will show. Trust in your own strength and prepare for the coming conflict.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_723.context: You will fight strong enemies coming at you. Their forces and vehicles are weak compared to the Pandavas' great army.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_725.meaning: Adapt your plans to the times. Making wise decisions now will bring you long term joy and success in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_725.context: Plan everything according to the current age. You will find lasting happiness and success if you follow this wise path.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_726.meaning: Leaders must act swiftly when the time is right. Quick decisive communication is essential during critical moments of action.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_726.context: King Susharma led the chariots. When the moment arrived he spoke his words very quickly to his troops.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1672.meaning: Beauty and celebration return when we honor the divine presence in our lives with joy and respect for tradition.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1672.context: A scene describes maidens surrounding the north while calling for a dancer to wear fine clothes and jewelry again.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1673.meaning: True happiness comes from celebrating together with music and gratitude, feeling proud of our shared spiritual heritage and unity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1673.context: People hear the earth speak and raise their hands in praise while playing drums and trumpets with great pride.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1674.meaning: Victory comes from inner discipline and focus, showing that controlling your mind leads to success in all endeavors.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1674.context: A speaker explains that the son conquered enemies because he mastered the great sound or vibration of the universe.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1675.meaning: We should embrace the beauty of life and ritual, allowing joy and splendor to uplift our spirits and surroundings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1675.context: The north is filled with maidens as they urge the great dancer to adorn himself with beautiful dresses and ornaments once more.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1676.meaning: Trust and faith between people can overcome doubt, showing that willingness to help depends on mutual belief and connection.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1676.context: A speaker hesitates to promise a happy day but agrees to help if the other person truly believes in their ability.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1677.meaning: True generosity means giving freely without holding back, showing that wealth is meant to be shared with everyone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1677.context: A person offers cows, gold, and all wealth, stating they have nothing to protect from giving away even to distant others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1678.meaning: Everyone makes mistakes, even divine beings, so we must stay humble and careful to avoid repeating common errors.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1678.context: A king is asked about his faults, with the reminder that even gods have flaws, so one should avoid them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1679.meaning: Leadership is strongest when supported by loyal family, showing that unity and prosperity grow through shared responsibility and love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1679.context: Someone asks if Sharutas saw the Pandavas, noting that Yudhisthira ruled a rich kingdom with his brothers by his side.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_351.meaning: He shows admiration, asking her to worship him when he falls, reflecting pride.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_351.context: Nahusha, a king of gods, meets a beautiful woman and praises her.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_352.meaning: He uses gentle imagery to flatter her, showing respect and admiration.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_352.context: Nahusha speaks to the pure goddess, comparing her to a banana tree in wind.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_353.meaning: He acknowledges her devotion, yet remarks on her fearsome look, hinting at humility.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_353.context: The goddess bows to Brahma, then Nahusha comments on her appearance.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_354.meaning: She seeks guidance, showing uncertainty and the need for divine help.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_354.context: The goddess asks Nahusha for something, unsure of Indra’s whereabouts.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_355.meaning: He promises honesty but his pride may cloud his judgment.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_355.context: Nahusha says he will reveal truth to the goddess, becoming proud.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_356.meaning: He reminds her of honesty, encouraging her to keep faith in reality.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_356.context: Nahusha speaks to the goddess, urging her to remember truth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_357.meaning: She finds liberation and seeks wisdom from the wise teacher.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_357.context: The goddess is freed by Nahusha and goes to Brihaspati’s home.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_358.meaning: They express worry, showing that even divine beings face concerns.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_358.context: Vishnu meets the gods and the eloquent women speak anxiously.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1165.meaning: When people break moral rules and sacred duties, it causes widespread damage and suffering for everyone around them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1165.context: Bad marriages and ignoring sacred laws cause harm to many different groups of people in society.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1166.meaning: Attacking spiritual leaders and their teachings destroys the moral foundation that protects and guides society.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1166.context: Harming holy teachers and stealing sacred knowledge leads to the downfall of other communities and clans.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1167.meaning: Conflict and theft within the spiritual community create chaos that negatively impacts the wider population.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1167.context: Fighting among religious scholars and stealing their wisdom causes destruction for other groups of people.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1168.meaning: Wealth differences create social gaps where poor families feel left out and excluded from the community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1168.context: Some families have many cows while others are poor and cannot join the main group.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1169.meaning: Even those with less wealth desire respect and try to gain fame within their social groups.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1169.context: Poorer families are left out of the main circle but still seek recognition and status.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1170.meaning: Keep peace in your home by being honest, loyal to friends, and kind to all visitors.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1170.context: We must avoid hatred in our family and never betray friends or lie to guests.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1171.meaning: Reputation has power to help or harm spiritual leaders and can impact the prosperity of the land.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1171.context: Fame can bring blessings or curses to the priests and affect the health of the land.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1172.meaning: Living with honesty and respecting the natural world ensures your home remains secure and peaceful.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1172.context: Nature elements and truth are the foundation that keeps a household safe and stable.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1256.meaning: You must follow moral rules to find real success because goodness is the only source of lasting happiness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1256.context: The text teaches that true wealth comes from following right conduct and moral duty in life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1257.meaning: When you stop doing bad things and focus on good deeds your spirit becomes pure and truly wise.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1257.context: This verse describes a person whose soul is free from bad actions and focused on doing good.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1258.meaning: You should pursue duty money and pleasure in balance so you find success in this life and the next.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1258.context: The passage explains how to balance duty wealth and desire at the right time in life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1259.meaning: Master your anger and excitement so your body stays healthy and your mind does not get confused by power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1259.context: This verse advises controlling strong emotions like anger and joy to keep the mind clear and calm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1260.meaning: Your inner strength comes from your family history so you should act with the noble power they gave you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1260.context: The speaker reminds the king that his strength comes from his noble ancestors and their legacy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1263.meaning: Do not hold hate against those who hurt you because creating enemies only brings more trouble to your life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1263.context: The text warns that being hurt by someone else should not lead to holding a grudge or hate.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1265.meaning: Be careful who you trust because even those who seem close can betray you for their own pleasure.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1265.context: This verse lists groups like women kings and snakes as people who are hard to fully trust.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1266.meaning: Respect dangerous forces in life like family conflicts because ignoring them can lead to serious harm for you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1266.context: The passage compares dangerous things like snakes fire lions and family members to bright horses that need care.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2792.meaning: True greatness shines so brightly that it naturally draws the attention and admiration of everyone around you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2792.context: Krishna arrives at the royal court with such beauty that no one else compares to him there.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2793.meaning: When you carry inner peace and strength, others will naturally respect you and make space for you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2793.context: People on the road felt small and stepped aside as Krishna passed by with his divine presence.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2794.meaning: Great events bring many people together, showing how shared joy can fill a place with energy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2794.context: Crowds of beautiful women filled the streets, creating a heavy and lively scene around the visitor.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2795.meaning: Even when surrounded by chaos and confusion, keep moving forward with purpose and steady determination.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2795.context: Krishnas horses moved along the path, surrounded by crowds that made it hard to see clearly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2796.meaning: Present yourself with dignity and purity, as your inner light reflects in your outward appearance and actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2796.context: Krishna entered the palace holding an umbrella, looking pure and beautiful with eyes like lotus flowers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2797.meaning: Face difficult situations with quiet strength and courage, knowing that your inner power guides your steps.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2797.context: He walked through the palace rooms with great power, approaching the blind king with calm confidence.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2798.meaning: Always act with fairness and integrity, letting your moral compass guide your interactions with others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2798.context: Krishna acted with perfect righteousness among the kings, showing his mature wisdom and divine duty.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2799.meaning: Stay true to your values even in powerful circles, as honesty builds trust and respect among leaders.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2799.context: The Lord maintained his righteous conduct among the rulers, demonstrating his role as a wise guide.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2833.meaning: True strength comes from doing the right thing, even when your body looks tired or weak from hard times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2833.context: A speaker praises Yudhisthira for his good character and asks why he looks so weak and thin.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2834.meaning: Loyalty and love between partners remain strong even when facing dangerous enemies or difficult challenges in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2834.context: The text describes fierce warriors and mentions how the Pandava brothers were always dear to their wives.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2835.meaning: Sometimes you must be brave and strong to protect those you love from those who wish them harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2835.context: This verse refers to Bhima killing Keechaka and describes his fierce nature as a protector of his family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2836.meaning: Great power and speed are gifts that can be used to defeat evil and protect the innocent people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2836.context: The speaker compares a warrior to powerful gods like Indra and Shiva, highlighting his speed and anger.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2837.meaning: Grief can make us feel lost and desperate, showing how deeply we care for the people we love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2837.context: A character expresses deep sorrow and wishes never to see Nakula again due to the pain of separation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2852.meaning: Being alive without your loved ones feels empty and painful, reminding us to cherish every moment together.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2852.context: A wife describes the moment she lost sight of her husband Nakula and expresses her deep unhappiness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2853.meaning: True beauty comes from having a good heart and strong moral values, not just from looking pretty.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2853.context: The speaker praises Draupadi for her beauty and noble character, noting she possessed all the best virtues.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2854.meaning: Staying true to your promises and duties shows great strength of character and deep loyalty to family.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2854.context: Draupadi is described as truthful and loyal, choosing to stay with her husbands instead of her sons.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2914.meaning: Belief in God gives life meaning; trusting Him brings peace and certainty in everyday life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2914.context: A devotee speaks of God as the source of all, affirming faith in divine truth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2915.meaning: Respectful invitation shows kindness; returning home reminds us to honor family and responsibilities.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2915.context: Govinda invites a woman, while Duryodhana returns home after a brief visit.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2916.meaning: Sharing gifts builds friendship; visiting others strengthens community bonds and mutual support.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2916.context: Govinda invites Pritha, gives gifts, and Duryodhana visits Shaurir’s house.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2917.meaning: Great wealth attracts attention; humility and respect are needed when encountering powerful people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2917.context: Purandara compares a house to a rich palace; doctors enter and pause in awe.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2918.meaning: Challenges rise like mountains; perseverance helps us reach higher goals despite obstacles.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2918.context: A mountain rises like a cloud; Sharia climbs a burning palace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2919.meaning: Powerful leaders gather to decide; wise leadership requires listening to many voices.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2919.context: Many kings surround the Kurus; Dhritarashtra sits on a throne.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2920.meaning: Friends gather to plan; loyalty and teamwork are vital for achieving shared aims.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2920.context: Dushasana, Karna, Shakuni, Saubala, and Tan sit near Duryodhana.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2921.meaning: Acknowledging leaders shows respect; worshiping wisdom guides people toward good decisions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_2921.context: Dasarha announces Dhritarashtra’s arrival; ministers worship Madhusoodana.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3088.meaning: Even after great loss, true happiness comes from remembering the purpose of fighting and the value of life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3088.context: A king asks the Pandavas about the joy found after many warriors die in battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3089.meaning: Courage grows when we stand together, trusting our allies to protect us from fear.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3089.context: Brave warriors feel fear, yet they are ready to fight for the Pandavas and Tavakasha.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3090.meaning: War takes many lives, reminding us that strength alone does not guarantee survival.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3090.context: The battle shows that many Kurus and Pandavas die, especially the thin fighters.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3091.meaning: Unity among leaders can prevent chaos, but anger can still lead to destruction if not controlled.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3091.context: Great kings gather, angry people threaten to destroy them all.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3092.meaning: Leadership means caring for others, ensuring safety, and guiding them toward a better future.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3092.context: A king is urged to save the world and protect his people from destruction.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3093.meaning: Good leaders are kind, honest, and respectful, showing that true power comes from virtue.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3093.context: Describes rulers as white, generous, green, noble, and pious.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3094.meaning: Peaceful gatherings help heal divisions, showing that sharing and unity restore harmony.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3094.context: Shiva brings rulers together to share food and drink, returning them home.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3095.meaning: True strength lies in using power wisely, turning conflict into peace and respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3095.context: A king is praised for his fine clothes and for calming enemies with his anger.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3266.meaning: Even distant people recognize the value of strong, long-lived leaders who bring honor to their family.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3266.context: Garuda’s sons are mentioned in a foreign land, known for great importance and long life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3267.meaning: When people ignore your needs, it is better to move on and seek a place that respects your preferences.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3267.context: Someone says, if you are not interested, we will leave and find a place that suits your taste.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3268.meaning: Hidden places can hold precious gifts, reminding us that beauty and value often come from unexpected sources.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3268.context: The seventh underground level, Rasatala, is where a fragrant mother of cows made from nectar is born.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3269.meaning: Nature takes what it needs, showing that sharing resources keeps the world balanced and healthy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3269.context: The earth constantly drains the milk made from the essence of six different juices, which is considered very good.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3270.meaning: True purity can arise from simple, honest actions, and it brings new life into the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3270.context: In the past, he was satisfied with nectar, then released a pure essence, and a blameless woman emerged from her grandfather’s mouth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3271.meaning: What we give to the earth can become a precious gift, showing that generosity is highly valued.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3271.context: Milk falls to the ground, creating a treasure that is sacred and excellent, made by Harada.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3272.meaning: Even in simple surroundings, wise people find nourishment and knowledge, proving that learning is everywhere.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3272.context: The foam is wrapped like a flower, and wise sages lived here, drinking and learning.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3273.meaning: Guarding all directions with care teaches responsibility and the importance of protecting what is important.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3273.context: He had four cows in all directions, living with guardians of the directions, remembered for holding them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3313.meaning: True beauty comes from having a kind heart and strong moral values, not just looks.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3313.context: A father describes his daughter as the most beautiful woman alive, full of good character.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3314.meaning: Good actions and family love create a happy home where children grow up well.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3314.context: A father praises his daughter and her husband, noting that their grandson is very handsome.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3315.meaning: We should pray for good luck and virtue to remain in our homes always.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3315.context: A prayer asks for the goddess of wealth to stay in the family forever.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3317.meaning: Parents should make choices that help their children and grandchildren have a good life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3317.context: Someone advises a father to give his daughter to a worthy man for the grandson.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3318.meaning: We should treat people with honor and respect when they show good intentions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3318.context: A king offers his daughter in marriage, saying the suitor deserves great respect.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3320.meaning: Sometimes we must say no to offers that do not fit our values or needs.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3320.context: A sage disagrees with a proposal, feeling the match is not right for the family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3322.meaning: Fear can make us act badly, but we should try to stay brave and honest.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3322.context: A speaker admits their argument is weak because they are afraid of a powerful enemy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3323.meaning: Bad news can spread quickly, so we must be careful about what we share.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3323.context: A message is passed along saying a powerful being will eat someone next month.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3324.meaning: We learn that harsh words can hurt our joy, and we should speak kindly to keep happiness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3324.context: A warrior feels sad after hearing harsh words from a friend named Suparna.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3325.meaning: Good plans and close family help us feel safe and confident in difficult times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3325.context: Matali tells someone that he has created a smart plan and that a beautiful son is nearby.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3326.meaning: Seeking help from wise leaders can guide us when we face confusing or dangerous situations.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3326.context: A serpent and Narada go to a powerful god to ask about a wise man named Vasava.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3327.meaning: Learning from others and helping friends shows true strength and kindness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3327.context: A hero promises to learn from others, live well, and help a bird named Garuda.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3328.meaning: Working together with trusted helpers can make difficult tasks easier and more successful.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3328.context: A prayer asks a god to help a child and a serpent to finish a task together.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3329.meaning: Seeing a powerful leader inspires courage and reminds us that great leaders protect and guide us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3329.context: Strong warriors look at a beautiful face and see the king of gods, Indra, sitting.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3330.meaning: Having a wise guide like Vishnu helps us understand important truths and act wisely.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3330.context: Lord Vishnu, with four arms, is present, and Narada tells Matali everything about the plan.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3331.meaning: Seeking blessings and strength from higher powers helps us become better and more resilient.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_3331.context: Vishnu speaks to a ruler named Purandara, asking for nectar to make him strong like immortals.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4156.meaning: Accept that life ends for everyone. Do not fear death because it is a natural part of the cycle of existence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4156.context: Yama represents death and justice. The text describes how all living beings eventually face their end like fruit falling.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4157.meaning: Do good deeds to bring joy to your family. Noble actions lead to lasting happiness and a respected legacy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4157.context: Heroes who do great deeds gain honor. Their families rejoice and they earn a place among the gods in heaven.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4158.meaning: Use your talents to help others. Hard work brings respect in this life and peace in the next.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4158.context: A warrior uses his strength and skills to fight. This brings him fame now and a good place after death.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4159.meaning: Stay brave and keep your duty. Quitting your responsibilities leads to a life without purpose or honor.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4159.context: The speaker warns against losing courage. Giving up manhood or duty leads to a path of emptiness and regret.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4160.meaning: Speak with care and truth. Your words carry weight and can heal or harm people deeply.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4160.context: Words have power and meaning. They cannot be ignored or treated lightly like simple medicine that fails to heal.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4162.meaning: Do not trust blindly in false security. Be wise and prepared for trouble instead of waiting for it.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4162.context: Some people trust the sea king blindly. They are weak and foolish, waiting for disaster to strike them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4163.meaning: Lead by example with action. People will follow you when they see your dedication and bravery.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4163.context: He started working with a helper. Others will follow his lead when they see his strength and courage.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4164.meaning: Face challenges head on. Do not chase immortality but focus on living a brave and meaningful life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4164.context: Fight the enemy and move to safety. Wanting to live forever is impossible and not the true goal.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4389.meaning: Knowing your strong supporters and their special skills helps you feel ready for big challenges.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4389.context: Arjuna lists powerful allies and their unique weapons before the great war begins.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4390.meaning: Recognizing the strength and fame of others helps you respect their power and status.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4390.context: The speaker praises the mighty kingdom and its famous warriors to Krishna.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4391.meaning: A strong group of brave people can face any danger together with courage.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4391.context: More fierce warriors are named, showing the large army gathering for battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4393.meaning: Using special tools or wisdom given by higher powers can help you succeed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4393.context: Divine weapons blessed by gods are mentioned as part of the arsenal.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4394.meaning: Family members who are strong and loyal can provide great support in hard times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4394.context: The text mentions powerful relatives and their roles in the upcoming conflict.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4395.meaning: Being brave and loud like a tiger shows you are ready to fight.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4395.context: A very strong warrior is described as roaring like a tiger in battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4396.meaning: Loud noises and energy can show that a big event is about to happen.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4396.context: The loud sounds of war instruments fill the air before the fight starts.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4398.meaning: Working together with a sibling can make you both stronger and more effective.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4398.context: Two brothers are named as skilled warriors who will fight well.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4482.meaning: When things are falling apart, people often stop listening and cannot hear the truth anymore.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4482.context: The world is ending and the speaker feels their words cannot reach the listener's heart.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4483.meaning: When the end is near, fear takes over and we lose the ability to imagine a better future.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4483.context: A parent warns their child that total destruction is coming soon and no new hope appears.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4484.meaning: Even in the worst times, true strength and heroism can remain steady and unbroken by fear.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4484.context: A warrior sees Krishna standing strong and alive in the middle of a chaotic and dangerous forest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4485.meaning: We fear losing our chance to reunite with loved ones if we do not act rightly now.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4485.context: The speaker worries that if this meeting fails, they will not meet Krishna in heaven again.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4486.meaning: Sometimes we need to step back from a situation to find peace and clarity of mind.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4486.context: Karna hugs Krishna who is sad, then Krishna leaves the chariot to calm down his mind.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4487.meaning: When we fight with anger, we lose our wisdom and the true value of what we know.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4487.context: The speaker sees flaws in the battle plan and fears that knowledge is being destroyed by war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4502.meaning: We often worry about the safety of our leaders and elders when danger is close by.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4502.context: The speaker mentions old teachers and feels deep fear for the safety of the king's family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4503.meaning: True teachers choose kindness and peace over conflict, even when it is hard to do so.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4503.context: A teacher refuses to fight his own students because he loves them and wants to keep peace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4683.meaning: Strong bad feelings can stick to you and cause more harm if you do not let them go.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4683.context: A character speaks about a deep anger that will not go away easily.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4684.meaning: Sometimes we must face hard times, and it is good to know what happened before.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4684.context: Kings are moving their armies to the battlefield to fight a great war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4685.meaning: People often fight to keep control, and this struggle leads to the end of many lives.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4685.context: A speaker tells Arjuna that kings will fight hard to keep their power.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4687.meaning: It is important to remember what has already been said so you understand the whole situation.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4687.context: The speaker reminds the listener that they already know the full story of the meeting.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4688.meaning: Organizing your resources well helps you succeed in big tasks and reach your goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4688.context: A leader asks for his large army to be split into seven groups.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4689.meaning: Knowing the names of heroes helps us remember their strength and the people they loved.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4689.context: The text lists the names of seven famous warriors who are husbands of great women.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4690.meaning: Even the strongest heroes must eventually face death, reminding us that life is temporary.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4690.context: The story names three very strong warriors who have now died in the battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4691.meaning: Being skilled and disciplined in your work helps you handle any challenge that comes your way.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4691.context: The warriors were brave, learned, and very good at using many different types of weapons.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4749.meaning: Leaders must show courage and confidence to inspire their people before facing any major challenge or battle.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4749.context: The Pandava army entered the battlefield and blew their conches to signal the start of the great war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4750.meaning: True strength and unity can create a powerful presence that fills the hearts of your allies with joy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4750.context: The sound of the five Pandava brothers was so loud it felt like a fire blast to everyone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4751.meaning: When you act with boldness and purpose, your voice can reach far beyond your immediate surroundings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4751.context: A mighty warrior made a roar like a lion that echoed across the land, sea, and sky.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4752.meaning: Sometimes you must stand firm and close to your problems to face them directly and honestly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4752.context: King Yudhisthira set up his camp in a place that was equally close to the enemy forces.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4753.meaning: Conflict often forces us to leave behind our peaceful and sacred spaces to deal with difficult realities.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4753.context: The armies moved away from sacred temples, cemeteries, and the quiet homes of holy sages.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4754.meaning: Choosing a good and peaceful environment helps you build a strong and happy foundation for your life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4754.context: Yudhisthira chose a dry, sweet, and holy spot to build his camp and settle his people.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4755.meaning: True peace comes from being supported by a large and loyal community of friends and allies.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4755.context: The king rested happily while being surrounded by hundreds of thousands of other rulers and kings.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4756.meaning: Working together with a trusted partner allows you to overcome obstacles and protect what matters most.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4756.context: Krishna and Arjuna moved around the battlefield to drive away the enemy soldiers of Dhritarashtra.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5407.meaning: True strength comes from keeping your promises and staying focused on your goals, even when alone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5407.context: Hotravahana tells a young boy that his father Rama is living alone in the deep forest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5408.meaning: When many people respect and honor someone, it shows that person has great inner peace and power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5408.context: Many holy people and divine beings worship Rama every day on the great mountain called Mahendra.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5409.meaning: Showing respect to wise elders and sending kind messages helps build strong and loving family bonds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5409.context: The speaker asks a child to deliver a message to his father and bows respectfully to the ascetic.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5410.meaning: Trusting a good friend to help you with your problems brings peace and solves your worries.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5410.context: A man tells a gentle lady to share her decision with Rama, who will help her.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5411.meaning: Real friendship means knowing someone is brave, skilled, and always ready to stand by your side.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5411.context: The speaker describes Rama as his dear friend and a mighty warrior son of Jamadagni.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5412.meaning: Even old age does not stop you from doing your duty, and community support makes tasks easier.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5412.context: Thousands of sages stand up, and an old king named Srinjaya carries the sacred fire offering.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5414.meaning: Sharing stories and sitting together in a group helps people feel connected and understand each other better.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5414.context: People living in the forest ask each other questions and sit together in a circle to talk.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5415.meaning: Sharing happy stories with others can lift everyone's spirits and create a feeling of shared joy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5415.context: The speakers tell delightful stories to the king, and everyone there feels full of joy and happiness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_5553.meaning: This image shows purity and readiness for duty. It teaches us to prepare ourselves with clean hearts for important tasks.
